title: One source's verification
description: workareas/<workarea>/distil/verify/<source slug>.json: a verdict on every claim in the source's extract, written by agents that did not write the extract, plus any claim the extract missed. A long extract is verified in parts: each verify agent takes a range of claim ids and writes verify/<source slug>.part<N>.json in this same shape, and `tim distil merge-verify` joins the parts into the one file. `tim distil check --stage verify` validates it against this file, and also checks what a schema cannot: `source` names this file's source, `extractHash` matches the extract as it stands, the verdict ids are exactly the extract's claim ids, each once, and every missed id is <claim id>-m<N> for a claim in the extract, each once.

source.description: The source id from sources.json, such as "confluence:6518997274".

extractHash.description: The sha256, in hex, of the extract's claims array as canonical JSON (compact, every object's keys sorted), which ties the verification to the extract it judged. `tim distil merge-verify` writes it into the merged file; a part file leaves it out. `tim distil status` and `check --stage verify` need it in the merged file and count the source stale when it is missing or the extract's claims have changed since, even under the same ids. `tim distil adopt` records it for a verification written before extract hashes existed.

verdicts.description: One verdict per claim in the extract (or, in a part file, per claim in the part's range).

missed.description: Claims the source makes that the extract left out, each in the extract's claim shape. [] when nothing was missed.

text.description: Text that is not empty or only whitespace.

verdict.description: Whether one claim survives an attempt to refute it. The default is refuted, unless the quote is in the source and the statement follows from it.

id.description: The claim id from the extract.

holds.description: true keeps the claim in the working set. false drops it.

reason.description: Why it holds or does not, such as where the quote was found or what the statement overreaches.

claim.description: A missed claim, in the extract's claim shape (extract.schema.json). Its id is the nearest extract claim's id plus -m1, -m2 and so on, such as "conf-005-m1".

id.description: The nearest extract claim's id plus -m<N>, such as "conf-005-m1".

statement.description: The fact, in plain English. For an inferred claim, it says why it follows.

kind.description: What sort of fact it is. A gap is a confidence, never a kind.

ref.description: Where in the source: a section, heading, table row, page file, or file and line for a repo.

quote.description: The source's own words, verbatim. Only a gap, where the source says nothing, may leave it empty.

confidence.description: verbatim: the source says it. inferred: read between the lines, and the statement says why. gap: the source should say something here and does not.

note.description: Anything else the verifier wants the reconciler to know about this claim.

then.description: A verbatim or inferred claim quotes the words it rests on.
